## Strategy
Use \(22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq4^4\) (the intended \(i=j=p=c=2\) case; “\((2,2,4,4)\)” is not itself a partition). Set
\[
B_d=\{(2,2,\rho):\rho\subseteq2^2,\ |\rho|=d-4\}\quad(4\le d\le8),
\qquad B_d=\varnothing\quad(d\ge9),
\]
and \(D_d=C_d\setminus B_d\).

For a row matrix \(M_d\), select rows \(P_d\) such that
\[
U_d=M_d[P_d,D_d]\in GL_{|D_d|}(\mathbb Z),\qquad T_d=M_d[P_d,B_d].
\]
For each complete Pieri row \(r\), verify the integral residual identity
\[
M_d[r,B_d]-M_d[r,D_d]U_d^{-1}T_d=0.
\]
Then every row is an integral combination of the selected rows. Hence the row lattice is the graph of an integral map over \(\mathbb Z^{D_d}\); its Smith data are \(|D_d|\) unit factors and a free quotient with basis represented by \(B_d\).

A fresh computation must enumerate all columns and complete \(h_1,\dots,h_4\)-Pieri rows, provide \(P_d,U_d,\det U_d\), and verify every residual without invoking an SNF routine.

## Gaps
The sole ledger artifact `fc00602a37cc13ac68bd15d11942922bcc608656e27d2ed99bc01f01ec08c914` computed Smith data directly. It contains no \(B_d,D_d,P_d,U_d\), determinants, or residual checks. Thus it does not test the stated block algorithm or establish that the full row lattice equals the selected-row lattice.

Completeness of the Pieri presentation also still needs the stated Schur/LR grounding and the project-context use of \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4)\).

**Requested target: not established.**

## Next
